stable_intent_contract: The request is solvable and the intended outcome does not change; no required user information is withheld to manufacture failure.

irreversibility: A delivered order becomes exchange requested or return requested after the first resolution write.
The opposite delivered-order resolution is rejected after the first write and the first write remains committed.
A pending item modification changes status and blocks a second item modification and cancellation.
policy_visible: The one-call exchange and pending-item-modification boundaries.
Allowed return payment destinations and gift-card timing.
The requirement to collect all item changes before committing.
missing_native_state_or_actions: No fulfillment-mode contract that changes which resolution preserves a user benefit.
No replacement-history state beyond terminal request fields.

candidates.name: FULFILLMENT_CONDITIONED_EXCHANGE_OR_RETURN
candidates.native_anchor: Exchange and return are both executable first writes on delivered orders and are mutually exclusive afterward.
candidates.minimal_extension: Expose a fulfillment_mode on delivered orders and add a stable v3-only contract for whether exchange preserves the original purchase protection. Return behavior remains native.
candidates.stable_user_goal_example: Exchange for the named variant if the original purchase protection will remain; otherwise return the named item to the stated allowed payment method. Do not take any other resolution.
candidates.latent_mapping: Observable fulfillment mode determines whether exchange preserves the required benefit, selecting exchange versus return.
candidates.counter_direction: At least one mode must require exchange and another must require return under the same conditional goal.
candidates.wrong_action_consequence: The wrong resolution call succeeds, changes the order to a terminal request state, and makes the preferred conditional goal unreachable.
candidates.ordinary_retry: Blocked by the native delivered-order status transition.
candidates.shortcut_risk: MEDIUM_HIGH: natural fulfillment labels may invite a correct guess; Gate 1 must establish real E0 headroom.

candidates.name: PAYMENT_PROVENANCE_REFUND_ROUTING
candidates.native_anchor: Return records one refund destination and accepts the original method or a gift card.
candidates.minimal_extension: Add mixed-payment provenance and deterministic routing semantics.
candidates.stable_user_goal_example: Return the named item set using the refund destination that satisfies the user's stated availability or timing need.
candidates.latent_mapping: Payment composition determines a routing action or allocation.
candidates.counter_direction: Different payment compositions must require different destinations or allocations.
candidates.wrong_action_consequence: A return request could commit with an incorrect refund destination.
candidates.shortcut_risk: HIGH: current tool accepts only one destination, so a richer rule risks becoming a task-specific lookup.

candidates.name: REPLACEMENT_HISTORY_RESOLUTION
candidates.native_anchor: Delivered-order resolution is terminal after one exchange or return request.
candidates.minimal_extension: Add visible replacement-history state and at least two executable history-sensitive resolution paths.
candidates.stable_user_goal_example: Resolve the named item to the requested outcome without losing the named entitlement.
candidates.latent_mapping: Replacement history selects ordinary exchange/return versus a distinct continuation path.
candidates.counter_direction: Fresh and previously replaced states must require opposite valid paths.
candidates.wrong_action_consequence: An ordinary path could commit and consume the remaining entitlement.
candidates.ordinary_retry: Potentially blocked, but the second valid continuation tool does not exist natively.

candidates.name: PENDING_MUTATION_ORDER
candidates.native_anchor: Pending item modification blocks a second item modification and cancellation.
candidates.stable_user_goal_example: Apply the requested changes to one pending order.
candidates.latent_mapping: Correct mutation order preserves reachability of all requested changes.
candidates.counter_direction: No clean reverse direction was found in which the opposite order is required.
candidates.wrong_action_consequence: A premature item modification can make later work unreachable.
candidates.shortcut_risk: CONFIRMED_HIGH: the public Policy explicitly tells the Agent to collect all item changes and warns about the one-shot transition.

candidates.name: PROMOTION_PRESERVING_REFUND_REORDER
candidates.native_anchor: Cancellation and return create refund state.
candidates.minimal_extension: Add promotions, promotion carryover, and a create-order or reorder action.
candidates.stable_user_goal_example: Obtain the named replacement while preserving the stated promotion.
candidates.latent_mapping: Order and promotion state select exchange versus refund and reorder.
candidates.counter_direction: Promotion states could require opposite paths.
candidates.extension_scope: VERY_HIGH: the required reorder path and promotion state are both absent.

candidates.name: SPLIT_FULFILLMENT_PARTIAL_RESOLUTION
candidates.native_anchor: Orders expose fulfillment groups and item membership.
candidates.minimal_extension: Would need fulfillment-scoped resolution transitions instead of the current order-wide terminal status.
candidates.stable_user_goal_example: Resolve the requested item set spanning fulfillment groups.
candidates.latent_mapping: Fulfillment grouping would determine batching or sequencing.
candidates.counter_direction: The current API supplies no case where splitting is required and safe; one combined call dominates.
candidates.wrong_action_consequence: A partial first call can strand remaining items.
candidates.shortcut_risk: HIGH: always submitting the complete item list is sufficient under the native API.

recommendation.reason: It reuses two real native terminal writes, needs only one visible order attribute plus one stable outcome contract, supports opposite correct actions, keeps the full user goal upfront, and blocks trial-and-error through native status transitions.
required_before_rollout: Implement the extension in a process-local v3 Retail subclass without modifying native Retail or Benchmark v2.
Use two matched delivered orders whose correct actions point in opposite directions.
Prove both correct paths and both wrong committed paths without model calls.
Keep fulfillment labels, benefit values, candidate order, and amounts from directly encoding the answer.
Reject the primitive if either fulfillment mode has a tool error before commitment or if E0 solves both tasks at ceiling.
